axes.model_access: Own model family (V3/V4 lines): the official API docs list model values (recraftv3 / recraftv3_vector etc.); closed-source, no open weights. The differentiator is **vector-native** — it can output real SVG files (official docs state the vector/SVG output line plainly).
axes.runtime: Web (recraft.ai) + API (external.api.recraft.ai, the endpoint in official docs); generation on the vendor's cloud. The official ComfyUI node is an API bridge (needs a key, online) — not offline weights.
axes.local_files: Works stored account-side in the cloud; SVG/PNG downloads go local. No officially stated local data surface.
axes.background: Generation is instant/queued (varies by account tier, not verified item by item); no "keep-running-after-shutdown" task surface (no claim verified); on the API side, batching runs on the caller's own concurrency.
axes.tools: The product includes a style library + custom brand styles (brand kit), inpainting/outpainting, background replacement, mockup generation, text placement (official docs: the V3 line is the only one that can place text precisely inside images); the full API operation surface is documented.
axes.context: Organized by projects; cross-session memory — no official statement verified. Brand styles are its "consistency" mechanism — reusable styles are not memory.
axes.permissions: Account + subscription system; free-plan works are public by default and not licensed for commercial use (official docs framing) — this is its most critical tier difference from most peers; paid plans grant commercial rights (D9: prices not collected).
axes.fit: Fits: design-oriented output (logos/icons/illustrations needing editable SVG), brand consistency (brand kit), precise in-image text layout. Does not fit: free commercial use (the free plan's no-commercial line is hard); a photorealistic-realism focus (it leans design).

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to creative products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **The editability quality of SVG output** (whether path structures are truly editable or bitmap tracing)
- **The actual stability of brand-kit style consistency**
- **The concrete meaning of the free plan's "public"** (whether works enter a public gallery)
unknowns:
- The display scope and withdrawal mechanism of free-plan publicity (not verified item by item)
- Cross-session memory mechanism (no official statement verified)
- The training-use switch (not verified line by line)
- Capability-difference details between the V4 and V3 lines (listed in API docs, not verified item by item)
related: Both design-oriented: Firefly embeds in the Adobe ecosystem, Recraft is a standalone vector-native bench.
Both strong in-image-type lines: Ideogram leads with typography-photo hybrids, Recraft with design vectors.
Design-asset downstream: Recraft outputs SVG, Figma MCP plugs the design files into agent toolchains (cross-linked after filing).
